A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CVFM/CVSFM research despite the changed title and organization. The complete 35-page v4 and 42-page v5, including their appendices, equations, tables and rendered figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original model evaluations on three synthetic mappings, MNIST–FashionMNIST transfer and simulated materials dynamics, including Tables 1–3 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v5 retains original experimental results and reports additional baseline, distributional-metric, kernel-sensitivity and computational-cost results in Table 1 and Appendices E and G.

M1.justification: The core CVFM/CVSFM components remain, but the written specification changes: v4 Equation (12) uses p-norms whereas v5 Equation (9) uses their p-th powers. The stochastic velocity in the algorithms also loses a denominator factor of 2. These are reported formula changes; corresponding implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: The established synthetic, image-transfer and materials coverage is retained. However, the new runtime study labels one mapping 'Moons to Gauss' in Figure G.1, whereas the earlier experiments and v5 Appendix D.3 specify Gaussians to Moons. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a reversed evaluation task or a labeling error.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds WFM and WFM-Entropic to the two discrete synthetic comparisons. T-COT-SFM(σy) loses its Table 2 row but remains in the appendix error-distribution comparison, so that comparator is not wholly removed.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces normalized path energy with Energy Distance and MMD while retaining Wasserstein-2 error. Appendix D.3 introduces conditional evaluation procedures for these metrics, including 16,384 samples and 200 equal-width conditioning bins for continuous cases. New kernel-sensitivity and runtime-versus-batch-size evaluations further expand the protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 adds comparisons of squared-exponential, Laplace and Cauchy kernels and a bandwidth sensitivity study. Appendix G adds runtime–accuracy comparisons of exact OT, Sinkhorn and kernel-only coupling. Existing η sweeps, kernel-only convergence comparisons and objective-variance results are retained or redisplayed, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed means and standard deviations in Tables 1 and E.1. The added results and plots do not establish a changed repeated-run count, uncertainty-estimation practice or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 extensively revises Wasserstein-2 values: CVFM on 8 Gaussians–8 Gaussians changes from 0.571±0.139 to 0.302±0.022. It removes path-energy results and adds ED/MMD and comparator entries. New kernel and runtime outcomes are reported. Table 2 omits T-COT-SFM(σy)'s numerical summary, although its error curves remain; other materials, image-transfer and variance table values are retained apart from rounding.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 replaces exact gradient equivalence with a mismatch-dependent error bound under explicit kernel and moment assumptions. Proposition 3.1 now handles unequal conditioning marginals and requires finite moments, rather than asserting an unconditional zero limit. Appendix A.3 replaces the earlier continuity argument with an ODE-based proof and a Wasserstein-distance bound.

C1.justification: Conditional density transport from unpaired observations and the Schrödinger-bridge extension remain the central contributions. v5 sharpens the claim around kernel stabilization in sparse continuous-conditioning regimes and withdraws v4's explicit conclusion that high-dimensional scaling has been demonstrated.

C2.justification: v5 adds a materials-specific stiffness and score-restoration explanation, kernel-tail and entropic-OT interpretations, computational tradeoffs, and limitations concerning bandwidth, conditioning geometry and high-dimensional instability. Some new interpretation exceeds the plotted evidence: Appendix F claims stability across bandwidths up to 10, while Figure E.6 shows variance reaching approximately the COT-FM level there.

D1.justification: v5 adds WFM encoder settings, ED/MMD implementation details and practical bandwidth/transport-penalty selection guidance in Appendix F. Hardware and the code URL are retained. Conversely, the unified algorithm no longer specifies the Sinkhorn regularization value of 2σx² given in v4 Algorithm 2.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially expands positioning against distribution-level MFM/WFM, multi-marginal conditional dynamics and Distribution-Conditioned Transport. It distinguishes CVFM through stability under sparse continuous conditioning and develops explicit arguments about competing frameworks' applicability, beyond v4's shorter discussion of concurrent conditional OT methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, background and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting. A dedicated Related Work section and Limitations subsection are introduced, the algorithms move into the main narrative, image transfer moves to the appendix, and the appendices gain a contents page and reorganized sections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced by a conceptual stability diagram; retained variance data receive new displays; and kernel-sensitivity and computational-cost figures are added. Table 1 is extensively restructured, v4 Figure 2 is split across main-text and appendix displays, and the two general algorithms are merged. The document also adopts a different publication layout.

improvement.justification: v5 improves theoretical qualification and adds useful metrics, kernel/runtime diagnostics and explicit limitations. However, it propagates a factor-of-two problem into the stochastic algorithms: their revised velocity conflicts with Equation (B.4) and the stated Brownian-bridge variance, whereas v4's algorithms retained the factor. The PDFs do not establish which implementation generated the results. Appendix F also overstates bandwidth robustness relative to Figure E.6. These correctness and interpretation concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the substantial additions.
